definition: An architecture with many specialized sub-networks (experts) plus a router that activates only a few per input.
details: MoE layers keep a huge number of parameters but compute with only a small subset for each token, so they can scale parameter count without proportionally scaling per-token compute. The sparsely-gated approach demonstrated this at massive scale; today many frontier LLMs use MoE to combine large capacity with efficient inference.
story: Think of an orchestra warming up: no single instrument carries the piece, but together they make the sound. Think of it this way: An architecture with many specialized sub-networks (experts) plus a router that activates only a few per input. And here is the clever part: MoE layers keep a huge number of parameters but compute with only a small subset for each token, so they can scale parameter count without proportionally scaling per-token compute. The shape of the machine is half the idea. And that shape of the machine — Mixture of Experts — is what makes everything else possible.

citation.title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
